context:
Goal: a test that fails only on Windows shows up before the batch, so it drops no batch.
Problem (rule): lane PRs are drafts and run no CI, so the only Windows run is the batch's. Each way to run Windows for each lane breaks a recorded ruling.
Based on (observed): draft lane PRs skip every job (run 42450467463, #1472).
Based on (observed): batch #1782 caught the T11b red in checks-windows, then was rebuilt without #1472.
Based on (ruling): decisions/draft-until-reviewed (owner, 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-13): CI skips drafts, and the batch run is the only CI run. Asked again because tonight a Windows-only red dropped #1472 from batch #1782 and forced a 48-lane rebuild, a cost that ruling did not weigh.
Departs from: decision draft-until-reviewed, where CI skips drafts — option a runs one Windows job on a draft lane PR. Option b instead departs from rule git-integration-branch-merge, one CI run per batch.
Meanwhile: lane windows-tests-for-touched-files (session_013NEJL4HeTtQTFg5s9G62RY) waits on this answer.

options.gain: Windows reds show on the lane, with no step by anyone.
options.how: checks.yml gets one job that runs on a draft PR, on Windows only, and runs only the test files the lane changed.
options.label: A draft-only Windows job runs just the test files a lane touches (recommended)
options.lose: One Windows job for each lane push that touches a test. It may queue behind or ahead of batch Windows jobs (unmeasured).

options.how: The lane dispatches one Windows workflow run on its head before it hands off to the batch runner.
options.label: The lane starts one Windows run on its head before hand-off
options.lose: A second CI run per lane, and harder from cloud sessions.

options.label: Keep today
options.lose: Windows-only reds keep dropping lanes and forcing batch rebuilds.

title: How should a lane's tests run on Windows before its batch?
why: The coordinator recommends a: it finds a Windows red on the lane with no manual step, and costs one job only when a lane touches a test.
